variables.reason: The candidate labels Ra as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations and assigns it a length dimension (L^1). The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness is the canonical definition for arithmetic mean roughness with symbols Ra / R_a and explicitly gives si_dimension: L and si_unit: m (domain: surface roughness). That record therefore directly defines the same physical quantity named Ra in the problem and supports every nonzero coordinate (the single length exponent) in the proposed SI vector.

The candidate defines kt as peak-to-valley height and assigns a length dimension. The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height is the canonical mean peak-to-valley roughness height (symbols include k_t, kt) and lists si_dimension: L with si_unit: m. That record corresponds to the same quantity in the original problem (peak-to-valley vertical height) and therefore supports the proposed SI vector having a single length exponent.

The candidate names k_rms as the RMS roughness height and gives it length dimension. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height is the canonical root-mean-square roughness height (symbols k_rms, krms) with si_dimension: L and si_unit: m. This entry defines the same RMS height statistic used in the problem, so it supports the single length exponent in the provided SI vector.

The candidate treats Sk as the standardized third central moment (skewness) and assigns it dimensionless. The KB record pq_height_skewness is the canonical surface-height skewness (symbols Sk, S_k), defined as the third standardized moment, and its si_dimension is listed as 1 (dimensionless). This record names and defines exactly the same statistical shape parameter present in the original problem and thus supports the all-zero SI exponent vector.

The candidate lists Ku as kurtosis and assigns it dimensionless. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis gives the canonical surface-height kurtosis (symbols Ku, K_u), defined as the fourth standardized moment, with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). That record corresponds to the same statistical measure in the problem and supports the proposed dimensionless SI vector.

The candidate defines ES as effective streamwise slope and sets it dimensionless. The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope is the canonical effective surface slope (symbols ES, E_x) defined as a mean absolute surface gradient (length/length) and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This record directly matches the ES quantity in the original problem and supports the all-zero SI exponent vector.

The candidate labels Po as surface porosity and assigns it dimensionless. The KB record pq_porosity (symbols Po, P_o, phi_p) defines porosity as a fraction (void fraction) with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless) and explicitly notes it as a surface porosity/void fraction. That record is the canonical source for the same Po used in the problem and therefore supports the proposed dimensionless SI vector.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The problem states to derive the dimensionless relationship governing the normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness ks/Ra using the given input parameters. ks/Ra is dimensionless as it is a ratio of lengths (ks and Ra). The input parameters include length scales (Ra, kt, k_rms), dimensionless shape factors (Sk, Ku), slope (ES), and porosity (Po). The dimensionless output ks/Ra is expected to be a function of these dimensionless and dimensional inputs, but itself is dimensionless.
